decisions.quote: Using 2007–2013 data from the United States, research by Fitzgerald, Schor, and Jorgenson lent support to this policy option by finding a positive and statistically significant relationship between average work hours and state-level CO2 emissions. We replicated their analyses by including more recent data and confirmed the linkage between the average hours worked in a state and annual overall CO2 emissions.
decisions.reason: The abstract explicitly states that the authors replicated the analyses of Fitzgerald, Schor, and Jorgenson on the relationship between average working hours and state-level CO2 emissions in the United States (originally using 2007-2013 data) by including more recent data (2014-2017). The blind coder only had the abstract and therefore recorded only the author surnames 'Fitzgerald, Schor, and Jorgenson' without year, title, or DOI. Shipped row input_row_index 47 (Fitzgerald, Schor, & Jorgenson, 2018, 'Working Hours and Carbon Dioxide Emissions in the United States, 2007–2013', Social Forces, doi: 10.1093/sf/soy014) is that exact original study.
